description:
A 'Rail Dial' ref. 1665 'Great White' Sea-Dweller. The Great White 1665 took over in 1977, with just the first two years in Rail Dial configuration. These dials marked the first instance of 'Sea-Dweller' appearing solo on the dial, axing the Submariner 2000 designation of its COMEX-bred predecessor, the Double Red. It is a massively capable dive watch built during an era when Rolex still treated its sport references as tools first, status symbols last.





Worth Reading:





The ref. 1665 Sea-Dweller rewrote the rules of what was possible with a dive watch. This ‘Great White’ marks the first time Sea-Dweller appeared solo on the dial, axing the Submariner designation of its COMEX-bred predecessor, the Double Red. In its place is stark, authoritative confidence in the Sea-Dweller as a separate model.  





Technically, this 1665 was relatively unchanged from the late evolution Double Red. It featured the patented helium escape valve at 9 o’clock, massively domed acrylic crystal, and 2000ft=610m depth rating that few would see. The 1665 was, by now, legend. It was born of saturation diving, engineered beyond the needs of nearly anyone who ever wore one, and built during an era when Rolex still treated its sport references as tools first, status symbols last. 





The Great White spanned production from introduced in 1977 until roughly 1983. Interestingly, this is roughly half as long as the Double Red. In this time, it spanned four dial ‘Marks’, each with its own character. This is a Mark 2 ‘Rail Dial’, a style briefly produced in the late 1970s for two years alone. It is so characterized by ‘Superlative Chronometer’ and ‘Officially Certified’ text alignment. Another unique detail of the ‘Rail Dial’ is the ‘T Swiss T < 25’ designation which no other Sea-Dweller presents. Why did Rolex revise the dial printing yet again and why did this version disappear so quickly? The answers aren’t always clear. That’s part of the appeal. 





This example from 1979 presents a beautifully-preserved dial with aged tritium which has hit a honey-tone with age. The Great White Rail Dial is not a 1665 which shouts like it predecessors. It is a variant which does not seek the spotlight. It rewards time, a little obsession, and research. Example like this very complete set are a delight to behold, for the case architecture, details, and history. Like most great vintage Rolex, it is the obsessives with trained eyes who most greatly delight in examples like this: not particularly rare, just excellent. 





Condition:





This 1665 presents in exceptional condition overall. The case here is peppered with light hairlines but has beautiful full proportions and sharp edges. All chamfers are full with sharp lug edges everywhere. Its dial sports lightly tan tritium, matching in the handset and under UV. Its calibre 1575 is running well in specification on our timing equipment. It comes with its full original set including punched papers, hang tags, manuals, and boxes.





Specifications:





This example is modelled on an average-sized 7-inch wrist.

A ref. 1675/8 GMT-Master with a rich matte brown 'nipple' dial and Oyster bracelet, beautifully preserved. The GMT-Master, initially developed for Pan Am pilots, is one of the great pillars of vintage sport Rolex. It was one of the earliest sport Rolex to embrace precious metal, a decision likely influenced by the heavily romanticized jet set culture in period. The 1675/8 brought a gold case into the updated and more robust successor to the model's initial reference, epitomizing the golden age of air travel.





Worth Reading:





The 1675 is without question one of the great pillars of vintage sport Rolex. Initially a tool for Pan Am pilots to track multiple time zones, it was born in an era when travel was heavily romanticized and the jet set were a well-heeled few. During this period, air travel was an exciting and novel event, passengers dressed for the occasion. This golden age of air travel likely inspired the GMT-Master to embrace precious metal, one of the first sport Rolex models to do so. While gold was available in the 6542, the 1675/8 brought the gold case into the updated and more robust successor to that initial reference. 





The 1675 added the practicality of an aluminum bezel and presided over the transition of gilt to matte dials. The color of the aluminum bezels was not painted but galvanically applied. It was also the reference that popularized the GMT-Master, where the 6542 was far smaller production and more fragile. Throughout production of the 1675, there are roughly 18 known dial variants. The 1675 was offered in both gold and two-tone with either black or brown dial. ‘Nipple’ indices were common to all, a distinguishing feature to further separate precious metal sport Rolex from their steel counterparts. 





The gold 1675/8 variant was produced at considerably lower volume than the steel 1675. This 1978 example features a beautiful matte brown dial and bezel, well suited to the warmth of the gold case with gilt print. While most 1675/8 were optioned with the jubilee bracelet this has a rarer oyster bracelet, considered a more sporting alternative at the time. 





A Gold GMT-Master perfectly exemplifies the time period in which the GMT was conceived. In period, the 1675 was very much a tool watch, though one for the elite. A gold variant was the ultimate display of status and jet set lifestyle. It is this reputation from which the modern GMT borrows its prowess, though it has become more symbol than tool. However, in the years following since, vintage gold with light wear and patina has taken on a different character. By contrast to today’s precious metal GMT-Masters, these read as almost subtle. Fortunately, these early examples still survive: a yellow gold tool watch born of the golden era of air travel.

             【Model Description】

The Daytona, which evolved from a tool watch to a status symbol in the previous generation, achieved further advancement in 2000 with the introduction of its first in-house chronograph movement, Cal. 4130.

Developed over five years, Cal.4130 inherited the exceptional fundamental reliability of the then-core Cal.3100 series. It eliminated hand jump during chronograph start-up and significantly improved chronograph running accuracy by adopting a vertical clutch chronograph mechanism.

Furthermore, the space freed up by the compact vertical clutch allowed for a larger mainspring barrel, achieving a 72-hour power reserve.

This generation, which evolved over more than 20 years with various additions, cemented the Daytona's reputation with its outstanding performance.

description:
Rolex Datejust 36 in Edelstahl und Roségold mit Jubilee-Band, schwarzes Zifferblatt mit arabischen Indexen, D-Serie aus ca. 2006, Rolex CPO Papiere aus 2024

 Datejust Bicolor

Gehäuse und Material

Die Rolex Datejust 36 Referenz 116231 kombiniert Edelstahl mit 18 Karat Roségold (Rolesor Everose) und verkörpert damit die klassische Eleganz der Datejust-Linie. Das 36-mm-Oyster-Gehäuse bietet ausgewogene Proportionen und hohe Alltagstauglichkeit. Die geriffelte Lünette aus Roségold setzt einen edlen Akzent und unterstreicht den ikonischen Charakter des Modells. Geschützt wird das Zifferblatt durch kratzfestes Saphirglas mit integrierter Cyclops-Lupe über dem Datumsfenster bei 3 Uhr.

Zifferblatt und Funktionen

Das schwarze Zifferblatt mit arabischen Indexen verleiht der Uhr eine markante und zugleich seltenere Ausstrahlung innerhalb der Datejust-Kollektion. Die applizierten Ziffern sorgen für eine klare Ablesbarkeit und bilden einen spannenden Kontrast zum dunklen Zifferblatt. Neben der Anzeige von Stunden, Minuten und Zentralsekunde verfügt die Uhr über die charakteristische Datumsanzeige mit Schnellverstellung.

Armband und Schließe

Die Uhr ist mit dem klassischen Jubilee-Band in Edelstahl und Roségold ausgestattet. Das fünfreihige Band bietet hohen Tragekomfort und unterstreicht den eleganten Charakter der Datejust. Abgeschlossen wird es durch eine verdeckte Crownclasp-Faltschließe, die sich harmonisch ins Design integriert.

Uhrwerk

Im Inneren arbeitet das Rolex Automatikwerk Kaliber 3135. Dieses bewährte Manufakturkaliber ist bekannt für seine Robustheit, Zuverlässigkeit und Präzision. Es verfügt über eine Gangreserve von ca. 48 Stunden und erfüllt die strengen Rolex-Normen hinsichtlich Ganggenauigkeit und Langlebigkeit.

Zustand und Zubehör

Die Uhr wird mit Rolex Certified Pre-Owned Papieren aus dem Jahr 2024 angeboten.

Besonderheiten & Historische Einordnung

Die Referenz 116231 stammt aus der D-Serie und wurde ca. 2006 produziert. Sie gehört zur Generation der modernen Datejust-Modelle mit klassischem 36-mm-Gehäuse und dem bewährten Kaliber 3135. Die Kombination aus schwarzem Zifferblatt und arabischen Indexen ist vergleichsweise selten und verleiht diesem Modell eine eigenständige Note. Durch die Rolex CPO Zertifizierung aus 2024 gewinnt diese Datejust zusätzlich an Attraktivität und dokumentierter Sicherheit hinsichtlich Authentizität und Qualität.

description:
The Oyster Perpetual Sea-Dweller in Oystersteel with a Cerachrom bezel insert in black ceramic and an Oyster bracelet. 



Legendary divers’ watch

The 60-minute graduated, unidirectional rotatable bezel of the Sea-Dweller enables divers to precisely and safely monitor their dive and decompression times.

It is equipped with a patented black Cerachrom bezel insert manufactured by Rolex in a virtually scratchproof ceramic whose colour is unaffected by ultraviolet rays. The graduation is coated via PVD (Physical Vapour Deposition) with a thin layer of platinum. The dial features large Chromalight hour markers and hands, filled with luminescent material that emits a long-lasting blue glow for excellent legibility in dark conditions.



Inspired by the original

The black dial of the Sea-Dweller has the large hands and indices reserved for Rolex professional models. The dial bears the name Sea-Dweller in red, a reference to the first model.

The innovative Chromalight display on the dial pushes back the boundaries of visibility in dark environments. Its distinctive blue glow lasts up to eight hours with a uniform luminosity, practically twice as long as that of standard luminescent materials.

description:
Rolex “ Small Crown” Submariner Reference 5508 





The reference 5508 is one of the most important early Submariners not because of what it introduced, but because of what it preserved. As the final no-crown-guard Submariner rated to 100 meters, it bridges the gap between the iconic 6538 and the more robust references that followed.  





A short-lived chapter from 1958 where its restrained dimensions, meters-first dial, and small crown make it a cornerstone for collectors who value historical continuity over excess. Quietly rare, deeply significant, and endlessly wearable, vintage Rolex doesn’t get much more honest than this. 





Please read the condition report carefully and refer to the high-resolution pictures to assess the overall condition of the watch. 





MODEL / REFERENCE: Rolex Submariner reference 5508. The 361XXX serial number and case back date the watch to the second quarter of 1958. 





DIAL + HANDS: The matte black dial appears to be an early Rolex service replacement. The lume markers developed a nice beige patina. The white printing remains intact throughout, including the chapter ring. 





The luminous hour markers and Mercedes hands have matured into a matching, warm vanilla color.  





CRYSTAL: The acrylic crystal is in fair vintage condition, showing various surface scratches that can be polished off. 





CASE: The 37mm Oyster case remains strong and well defined, with sharp lines and pronounced bevels along its thick, even lugs. It retains its correct finish and displays honest signs of use throughout, commensurate with age and use.  





The bi-directional bezel with aluminum insert shows various scars. The painted red triangle and luminous at 12 o’clock are likely original and remain intact. 





CASEBACK: Signed Oyster case back with correct period stamps and internal nomenclature.  





CROWN: Signed Rolex “Twinlock” crown, that closes securely and operates exactly as intended. 





MOVEMENT: Self-winding Rolex Calibre 1530. It has been checked, is fully functional and keeping good time. 





BRACELET: Rolex Oyster riveted bracelet, fitted with number 64 end links, a signed Jubilee clasp reference “6252H 14” and dated to the second quarter of 1971.  





ACCESSORIES: Saffiano leather watch roll.

Splendido Rolex GMT 6542, dial virato al marrone, inserto ghiera in Bakelite, completamente originale e coevo, Expertise di Carlo Pergola del 2024.



Il presente Rolex GMT-Master referenza 6542 è un esempio altamente evocativo del primissimo modello GMT mai prodotto dalla manifattura, introdotto a metà degli anni ’50 per i piloti della Pan American World Airways e oggi considerato uno degli orologi sportivi Rolex più iconici e storicamente importanti.



Questa prima referenza è immediatamente riconoscibile per il suo profilo sottile, l’assenza di protezioni per la corona e la caratteristica lunetta in bachelite che ha definito la prima generazione del GMT-Master. L’orologio conserva il suo inserto in bachelite, preservando l’estetica distintiva che ha reso il 6542 una pietra miliare nello sviluppo degli orologi strumento Rolex.



Il quadrante è invecchiato assumendo un ricco e attraente colore marrone tropicale, risultato di una trasformazione naturale e molto ricercata dal suo tono nero originale. Gli indici luminosi delle ore mostrano una riluminescenza successiva, eseguita con cura e in modo coerente con la patina generale del quadrante. Le lancette di primo tipo e la prominente lancetta GMT esemplificano ulteriormente il linguaggio di design unico della generazione inaugurale del GMT-Master.



Animato dal calibro automatico 1065 e corredato da un bracciale Jubilee corretto per il periodo, questo 6542 esprime pienamente il carattere e il fascino dei primi orologi Rolex legati all’aviazione.



In quanto referenza che ha inaugurato la linea GMT-Master, gli esemplari sopravvissuti restano eccezionalmente desiderabili, in particolare quelli che conservano la lunetta in bachelite e presentano un quadrante tropicale formatosi organicamente nel corso dei decenni. Questo orologio rappresenta un esemplare convincente, storicamente significativo e visivamente affascinante dell’era pionieristica di Rolex negli orologi da polso a doppio fuso orario.

description:
Rolex Cosmograph Daytona “Tiffany Turquoise”





Reference 126518LN – Yellow Gold Oysterflex





The Rolex Cosmograph Daytona ref. 126518LN with turquoise dial is one of the most eye catching modern Daytona executions, combining precious metal construction with a vibrant, contemporary dial color and Rolex’s most advanced chronograph movement. Produced in very limited numbers, this configuration has quickly become one of the most talked about modern Daytonas among collectors.





The watch features Rolex’s signature 40mm Oyster case crafted from 18k yellow gold, delivering both luxury and robustness. The case is topped with a black Cerachrom tachymeter bezel, engraved with gold filled numerals that are highly resistant to fading, corrosion, and scratches.





The standout feature of this reference is its turquoise blue lacquer dial, often nicknamed “Tiffany” by collectors due to its vibrant tone. The dial is paired with black sub dials, creating a striking reverse panda contrast that enhances legibility and visual depth.





Applied 18k gold hour markers and hands are filled with Rolex’s Chromalight lume, offering long lasting blue luminescence in low light conditions. The overall aesthetic is bold, modern, and unmistakably Daytona.





This model is fitted with Rolex’s innovative Oysterflex strap, a high performance elastomer strap reinforced with flexible metal blades for durability and comfort. It is secured by a yellow gold Oysterlock folding clasp, ensuring both security and ease of wear. 





Movement





Powering the watch is Rolex’s current-generation in house chronograph movement, Caliber 4131, introduced as part of the updated Daytona line.





    Automatic winding


    Column-wheel chronograph with vertical clutch


    Hours, minutes, small seconds


    Chronograph with central seconds, 30-minute and 12-hour counters


    Rolex Chronergy escapement


    Paraflex shock absorbers


    Frequency: 28,800 vph (4 Hz)


    Power reserve: approximately 72 hours


    Superlative Chronometer certified (−2/+2 seconds per day)





The vertical clutch ensures smooth chronograph engagement without hand jump, while the column wheel delivers precise, tactile operation of the pushers.

Rolex GMT-Master II Batgirl model 126710BLNR, in one of the most sought after and desired configurations on a Jubilee bracelet and the very popular black and blue ceramic bezel, with blue GMT hand.





This model features a black dial and a two-color Cerachrom bezel insert in blue and black ceramic. In addition to conventional hour, minute and seconds hands, the GMT-Master II features an arrow-tipped hand, which circles the dial once every 24 hours, as well as a bidirectional rotatable 24-hour graduated bezel.





The distinctively colored 24-hour hand displays the “home” reference time in a first time zone which can be read on the graduations on the bezel. The traveler’s local time is easily set by “jumping” from hour to hour, thanks to an ingenious mechanism operated via the winding crown: the hour hand can be adjusted forwards or backwards independently of the minute and seconds hands. This allows travelers to adapt to their new time zone without affecting the precision of their timekeeping.





Like all Rolex Professional watches, the GMT-Master II offers exceptional legibility in all circumstances, and especially in the dark, thanks to its Chromalight display.





The broad hands and hour markers in simple shapes – triangles, circles, rectangles – are filled with a luminescent material emitting a long-lasting glow.

We are proud to present this exceptional Rolex Oyster Perpetual Day-Date, Reference 18026, a highly coveted and historically significant example of Rolex’s most prestigious model, crafted in 950 platinum. Originally sold in 1980, this remarkable vintage Day-Date is offered in unpolished condition and accompanied by its original box and papers, making it an outstanding and increasingly rare full-set example for the serious collector.

The 36 mm platinum Oyster case remains exceptionally crisp, retaining its original factory lines, sharp edges, and proportions—clear evidence of careful ownership over the past decades. As one of the earliest platinum Day-Date references, the 18026 represents a pivotal moment in Rolex history, combining discreet luxury with unmistakable weight and presence on the wrist.

The watch features a superb diamond-set dial, offering a refined contrast against the cool tone of platinum. The applied diamond hour markers elevate the classic Day-Date aesthetic while maintaining excellent legibility and timeless elegance. Completing the signature layout are the day display at 12 o’clock and the date at 3 o’clock, both hallmark complications of Rolex’s flagship model. This reference is equipped with the single quick-set date, correct for its production era.

Powering the watch is the Rolex in-house automatic caliber 3055, a robust and reliable movement developed specifically for the Day-Date line. Renowned for its durability and precision, the movement reflects Rolex’s commitment to functional excellence and long-term reliability.

The watch is fitted with its original platinum President bracelet, further enhancing its exclusivity and unmistakable character. The bracelet remains in excellent condition, perfectly complementing the unpolished case and reinforcing the watch’s exceptional overall originality.

Die Datejust wurde damals als Uhr zur Feier des 40 jähriges Unternehmensjubiläum eingeführt und ist bis zum heutigen Tag Bestandteil der Rolex Kollektion. Bei Betrachtung der Bilder wird ersichtlich weshalb: Klare Strukturen, perfekte Qualität und eine Reputation in der Uhrenwelt, die kaum vergleichbar ist. 





Die Seriennummer lautet E334xxx. Das Jubilee Band mit 555er B Endlinks und 62510H Schließe ist mit O10 punziert. Verkauft wurde die Rolex im Januar Oktober 1991.





Der Durchmesser der Rolex beläuft sich auf 36mm. Die Rolex passt bis zu einem Handgelenksumfang von ca. 19,5cm.





Die Datejust befindet sich in einem sehr guten Zustand. Das Saphirglas ist kratzerfrei. Das Jubilee Band hat nur leichten altersbedingten Stretch. Bitte nutzen Sie die hochauflösenden Bilder als Referenz der Zustandsbeschreibung.





Die Rolex hat eine Revision im Dezember 2025 erhalten. Sie erhalten 12 Monate Garantie auf das Uhrwerk.

The new references did away with the ubiquitous aluminium bezel, instead offering a high-tech ceramic bezel that was much more resistant to scratches. 



The case and bracelet were also changed to make them feel much more substantial. While the original Submariners were created with pure practicality in mind, the Ceramic Submariners had an air of luxury appropriate appropriate for the 21st Century. 



Rolex's Submariner is to many the definitive wristwatch. From its origins as a diver's companion and James Bond's wristwatch, the Submariner has ingrained itself into popular culture like no watch before or since. Worn and loved by bankers, rappers and watch enthusiasts alike, the Submariner possibly the most culturally significant piece of horology ever.



This doesn't mean it's all talk and no action though - the Submariner is iconic for a reason. Its water resistant Oyster case, highly legible Mercedes hands and timing bezel may have originated as practical functions, but they've come together to create a beautifully proportioned watch that appeals as much to the designer's eye as it does to the procurement officer's spec sheet.

This is the new Rolex Submariner Date Ref 126610LN.


Black dial with 18ct white gold hour markers to prevent tarnishing. Unidirectional rotatable bezel with scratch-resistant Cerachrom insert in black ceramic. Oystersteel case with screw-down caseback and crown. Solid Oyster bracelet with Oysterlock folding safety clasp and Rolex Glidelock extension system.





The new 126610LN features a redesigned case. It’s larger (gasp!) at 41mm but the lugs are thinner and more tapered. Much like on the popular references from the 1990s/early 2000s.


The classic 3-link Oyster has also grown. By a full millimeter width along its entire length. It’s now 21mm between the lugs. According to Rolex though, this will ensure comfort on the wrist. And to be fair, there’s nothing worse than a thin-looking bracelet.





This Rolex is fitted with calibre 3235. 


The 3235 gets the Superlative Chronometer certification. Meaning it is very accurate (−2/+2 seconds per day) and reliable. It also features an instantaneous date at 3 o’clock with secure rapid-setting.

A piece of Rolex history, the Speedking made its first appearance in the 1940s and brought with it a classic design that is just as relevant today as it was when it first debuted. It was named after the “King of Speed” Sir Malcolm Campbell, a Rolex fan and breaker of speed records.





The quality and condition of this particular movement are nothing short of breathtaking, and it functions perfectly, running reliably and with excellent amplitude. By the late 1940s, Rolex had developed their production processes to almost an art form, and looking at this mechanism now with an eyeglass, we would find it difficult to class it as anything less than a working sculpture.
